what: Changes in ALK — extra copies, joins with another gene, or mutations — can help some lung cancers grow.
intro.test_report: If a test report mentions ALK, it is noting a finding about this gene. That note is not a diagnosis, and it is not a decision about treatment.

lines.text: Alectinib (Alecensa): a drug that blocks the ALK signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an ALK change. Authorised in Europe since 2016.
Brigatinib (Alunbrig): a drug that blocks the ALK signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an ALK change. Authorised in Europe since 2018.
Ceritinib (ZYKADIA): a drug that blocks the ALK signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an ALK change. Authorised in Europe since 2015.
Crizotinib (Xalkori): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for lymphoma with an ALK change. Authorised in Europe since 2012.
Ensartinib (ENSACOVE): a drug that blocks the ALK signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an ALK change.
Lorlatinib (Lorbrena): a drug that blocks the ALK signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an ALK change. Authorised in Europe since 2019.
